key_insight: HexFormer brings hyperbolic geometry into Vision Transformers by using exponential-map-based aggregation in attention, allowing transformer models to represent hierarchical and relational image structure more compactly and faithfully.
problem_solved: Current ViTs operate in Euclidean space, which struggles to encode tree-like or hierarchical relationships common in visual data; HexFormer addresses this by embedding and aggregating features on a hyperbolic manifold.
method: Embed patch tokens on a hyperbolic manifold and perform token operations in manifold-aware layers.
Replace standard attention aggregation with exponential-map-based aggregation that moves and combines vectors while preserving hyperbolic geometry.
Explore two architectural designs (e.g., a fully hyperbolic ViT and a hybrid hyperbolic–Euclidean variant) with manifold-aware parameterizations and training routines.
impact: Provides a practical way to inject inductive bias for hierarchies into Vision Transformers, yielding more compact representations and potentially improved accuracy/robustness on tasks with relational or hierarchical structure—useful for practitioners working on efficient or structured visual representation learning.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: Euclidean vs. Hyperbolic embedding spaces showing how hierarchical data is more compact in hyperbolic space.
Architecture sketch of HexFormer highlighting hyperbolic token embedding, exponential-map aggregation in attention, and output head.
Flowchart illustrating exponential map aggregation step (map to tangent, aggregate, map back to manifold).
Performance chart: accuracy or parameter-efficiency comparison (HexFormer vs. baseline ViT) and a t-SNE/Umap showing tree-like embedding geometry.
paper_title: HexFormer: Hyperbolic Vision Transformer with Exponential Map Aggregation
paper_authors: Haya Alyoussef, Ahmad Bdeir, Diego Coello de Portugal Mecke, Tom Hanika, Niels Landwehr
